sections.title: The checkerboard was never a model output
sections.lede: Redwood Elf asked why transparent background used to draw a grey-and-white checkerboard. ght901's answer is the one that belongs in the guide: the model never drew that pattern.
sections.body:
Redwood Elf (#nai-image-advice, Wed afternoon) had an old habit: ask for a transparent background and get a checkerboard. On V5 the same prompt looked different, and the sheer-silk clothing test got confusing fast — with Transparent BG on, the skirt stopped being partly see-through.

ght901: **"I don't think any of our models have ever given a checkerboard background when asked for a transparent background before."** On models before V5 it should have given a **white** background. And: **"very few models are capable of outputting images with transparency."** The checkerboard is how the UI *shows* alpha, not pixels the sampler painted.

luna (Thu) restated the older bug pair while the room joked about bringing bugs back: first, transparency accepted but unsupported → black background; second, transparency failing the signature check so Explore rejected the upload (the libwebp / alpha signature fix from Wednesday's changelog). New gens are fine; old transparent files stay unpostable until regenerated.

司 PhazonMadness tried `has alpha` / `alpha transparency` and a visual-novel sprite stack. Those tags help when the model *can* emit alpha; they do not invent a checkerboard.

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, 23 steps, guidance 5, Transparent BG toggle on:
`1girl, solo, standing, simple dress, transparent background, alpha transparency`
Download from the site (not clipboard). Open in an editor that shows alpha. Same seed with the toggle off and no transparency tags — white or solid bg, not a drawn checkerboard.

**CTA.** Confirm the downloaded PNG has a real alpha channel. Guide: §8 Two transparent-BG controls + Fri note.

sections.title: Explore downloads use the same filename builder as regular saves
sections.lede: Sigurd noticed Explore filenames switched to the Custom File Name Template shape. ght901 confirmed both paths call the same function.
sections.body:
Sigurd (#nai-diffusion-discussion, Thu ~01:22 ET): Explore downloads now look like `{date} {time} {(full model name and ID…)|upper} p-{prompt}` instead of the older `{prompt} s-{seed}` pattern — the same features that live in the Custom File Name Template under debug settings.

ght901: **"It does just use your settings. Both the regular download and explore call the same function for building the file name."** So if you tuned a template for gallery saves, Explore inherits it. No second secret naming path.

**Try this.** Set a Custom File Name Template you can recognise, download one gallery image and one Explore image, compare the names.

**CTA.** Frost/Menma: no contract change claimed; just note that Explore and download share the builder. Guide: §7 metadata / filenames.

sections.title: V4.5 could have been called V5 — we're 'on v6' in spirit
sections.lede: finetune and mahouko spent a minute on why the .5 naming stuck. Useful context when someone asks why V5 still feels like a bigger jump than the number suggests.
sections.body:
finetune (Thu morning): V4.5 **"really could have been called v5, considering how different it was from v4 in all regards. so we're, in a way, on v6. but it was a time of .5 models."**

mahouko: V4.5 **"had a lot of architectural stuff that we'd been cooking in preparation for v4.0 and which missed the boat"** — more **"v4 but with a later deadline"** than a half-step.

Not a prompting recipe. It does explain why community muscle memory from "just bump the version" keeps failing: the jumps were architectural, not label deep.

**CTA.** No lab ask — context for desk briefs when someone compares V4.5 → V5 to older half-steps.

sections.title: UC steers a look; a prompt-neg can delete the feature
sections.lede: Ifrit's lips example is the cleanest UC-vs-negative teaching moment this window. Vengyre's extreme feet pair shows what a huge UC negative looks like on the same seed.
sections.body:
Ifrit (#nai-diffusion-discussion, Wed): he stays on High because some custom UCs are **"too powerful if i converted them to neg."** Example: **"if i wanted to avoid bimbo lips, i can just uc it, but if u neg that, u get no lips."**

That matches the guide's field rule (prompt `-N::` suppresses; UC `-N::` un-suppresses / pulls toward tagged images) and gives a concrete failure mode: a prompt-neg on a body feature can erase the feature, while UC nudges the *style* of it.

Vengyre posted a same-seed pair: `-10::feet::` in UC versus none. Extreme weights are not a recommendation — Wednesday already pushed gentle `-0.25::` first — but the stills show how hard UC can shove.

Bicknell125 (Thu, mobile UI thread): **"medium does not have negative tags."** Restated from the effort-toggle week. If you need UC, use High (or put negative emphasis in the prompt on Medium).

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, 23 steps, guidance 5, one seed:
`1girl, solo, portrait, looking at viewer, soft smile, detailed face`
A: UC `exaggerated lips, glossy lips`. B: prompt `-1::exaggerated lips, glossy lips::`. Compare mouths.

**CTA.** Log which path keeps a normal mouth. Guide: §6 UC / negatives.

sections.title: Default quality tags pull you back to stock anime
sections.lede: J_the_Man's series style was drifting even with official-art anchors. Bicknell125's fix: turn QT off, write a stronger artstyle, or both.
sections.body:
J_the_Man (#nai-image-advice): for a consistent anime look he stacks `official art, anime screenshot, [series]` plus character `(anime)` tags and locks the seed — then watches the default-ish artstyle creep back in.

Bicknell125: **"the default quality tags will pull you that way if you're not building a strong artstyle prompt"** — **"you can either turn them off or construct a more complete artstyle or both."**

Same advice as mahouko's starter (QT off for full style control), now applied to a mid-session drift complaint rather than a cold start.

**Try this.** One seed, V5 Full High 23 guidance 5:
`1girl, solo, copyright:<series>, <character>, upper body, looking at viewer`
A: QT on. B: `append_quality` false. C: QT off plus a one-sentence artstyle (`a very high-quality anime screenshot style, smooth cel-shaded animation with vibrant colors and clean lineart` — Raezuto's unofficial clean-anime line, for lab only).

**CTA.** If B/C hold the series look and A drifts, bank it. Guide: §3 Automatic Quality Tags.

excerpts.speaker: J_the_Man
excerpts.text: Generally, if I'm making some image set, I've been using official art, anime screenshot, [series] plus character (anime) tags and locking the seed — then the default-ish artstyle creeps back in.

excerpts.speaker: Bicknell125
excerpts.text: the default quality tags will pull you that way if you're not building a strong artstyle prompt

sections.title: Hair length that tags won't pin: write the placement
sections.lede: J_the_Man could lock low twintails with tags but not the hair-down length he wanted. Raezuto's answer was a sentence.
sections.body:
J_the_Man wanted Nino Nakano's adult design at a specific hair length, then a hair-down version of *that* length. Tags like `medium hair, hair down` kept landing shorter than the twintail reference.

Raezuto: on V5, **"use straight prose to describe the placement of her hair/low twintails."** Example: `Her low twintails go over the front of her shoulders with the ends reaching her chest.`

Same pattern as Wednesday's borrowed-hairstyle prose (Uragan): tags name the character; a sentence places the detail.

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, 23 steps, guidance 5, character box:
`girl, <name>, blunt bangs, black hair`
Plus prose: `her hair hangs loose to mid-back, ends reaching below her shoulder blades.`
Compare to `medium hair, hair down` alone on the same seed.

**CTA.** Prefer the sentence when length/placement fights the tag. Guide: §8 Community notes Fri.

sections.title: Pokemon creatures: species: on furry, pokemon (creature) on anime
sections.lede: Bare pokemon does almost nothing. The room split the answer by dataset: furry wants species:, anime wants pokemon (creature).
sections.body:
dungeon_stockpot asked about mascot-like creature tags and got nonsense from bare `pokemon` / digimon stacks.

Gluttonous Beast: **"if you're just tagging `pokemon`, it obviously won't do much. You need a specific pokemon like pikachu."** On furry: `species:pikachu`.

ShameSoot: `species:pokemon, fakemon` **"veers things into a more cutesy friendly style"** and can pick up a Pokémon-like look without an artist mix.

司 PhazonMadness (anime): `pokemon (creature)` for creatures in general — plain `pokemon` is style/franchise. Example: `no humans, pokemon (creature)`.

**HOUSE reminder.** Furry mode is a `dataset_config` toggle (`include: ["fur dataset"]`, `furry_human` if needed). Never type `fur dataset` or the auto prefix into the prompt.

**Try this.** Anime path (no fur toggle): `no humans, pokemon (creature), outdoor, grass, daylight`. Fur path: enable fur dataset via JSON, then `species:pikachu, solo, standing`.

**CTA.** Same seed anime vs fur — don't stack dataset tags. Guide: §2 datasets + Fri notes.

sections.title: Side-by-side without the side-by-side tag
sections.lede: ShaddAI asked for another way to stand characters in a row. Redwood Elf posted a working pair that never used the tag.
sections.body:
ShaddAI: is there a prompt for characters standing in a row other than `side-by-side`? Redwood Elf answered with a still: **"It worked here, without 'Side by side' being involved."**

Not a universal substitute — boxes and positions still win for crowded casts (staff starter) — but useful when the tag fights the composition.

**Try this.** Two character boxes, positions left/right, base `2girls, standing, full body` and no `side-by-side`. Same seed with the tag on.

**CTA.** Prefer boxes+positions; treat the tag as optional.

sections.title: Behind the red wrapper: token spaces, realistic+ai-assisted, prompt-chunk weights
sections.lede: Unofficial technique that stays off the public billboard: V5's stricter token counting, a realistic polish pair, and how people organise weight stacks.
sections.body:
**V5 counts spaces and empty weights** (Aryllias, #nsfw-generation): **"Because v5 counts space and empty weights towards tokens. v4.5 and earlier, do not."** Tidy prompt chunks matter more; blank `::` scaffolding is no longer free.

**Realistic polish** (Nepsis): `realistic` alone is mild/glossy; **`realistic, ai-assisted`** together improves line flow, texture, and faces. Lower weight on `ai-assisted` if gloss is too much.

**Weight organisation** (Aryllias): higher in the chunk = higher weights, lower = lower — easier than hunting a stray tag. Same idea as keeping emphasised groups contiguous.

Raezuto also dropped clothing/hair `||randomizers||` and a clean-anime prose line in #nai-image-gen-discussion — useful, already mirrored lightly on the public QT/artstyle article.

**Try this (grim).** High, 23 steps: `realistic, 0.8::ai-assisted::, 1girl, solo, portrait, soft window light` vs `realistic` alone.

**CTA.** Lab free gens only; keep stills off the public grid. Guide: §8 Fri UNOFFICIAL notes.

excerpts.speaker: Aryllias
excerpts.text: Because v5 counts space and empty weights towards tokens. v4.5 and earlier, do not.

excerpts.speaker: Nepsis
excerpts.text:
Only thing needed to get that is ```Realistic, ai-assisted```

Realistic on its own is kind of meh. It takes the ai-assisted tag to really bring it together.

excerpts.speaker: Nepsis
excerpts.text: On its own it just makes things a little more glossy. When combined with the realistic tag, I feel like the lines flow better, textures seem better, and *especially* faces seem better IMO. It might help to lower focus on the ai-assisted tag if the glossiness is too much though.

excerpts.speaker: Aryllias
excerpts.text:
Higher up means higher weights. Lower means lower weights. 
It's easier to keep tags organized this way.
